title: ASCII Kinesis V2 Strikes 002 — Contact Pin / Disengage Before Recovery

source.name: Stanley Decker (Chainsaw)
source.rights_note: Copyright-restricted source used only as whole-sheet evidence. No source pixels, palette, exact contours, costume, frame layout, tracing, redistribution, or character-specific choreography are embedded or reproduced.
source.whole_sheet_boundary: The complete sheet was inspected as one corpus. It contains upright/retracted states, overhead tool states, multiple strongly forward-extended powered-tool attack drawings, and consequence/fall/destruction states. Static sheet order does not establish source chronology, exposure timing, a target contact instant, or hit-stop.

OBSERVED: the whole sheet contains both compact/retracted and strongly extended tool envelopes
multiple forward-extended attack drawings materially change torso and arm configuration while the tool remains committed forward
overhead and forward attack families create clearly different silhouettes and negative-space demands
non-attack and consequence states coexist with attack families
the source page reports Animated GIFs (0), so source-authentic exposure timing is unavailable
INFERRED: a generic powered-tool strike can treat contact as a short authored interval rather than a single point
during that interval the tool endpoint can remain spatially pinned while the body continues to compress behind it
recovery should first break the tool-contact relation before shoulders and root fully relax
support and bracing topology of the abstract rig
UNKNOWN: exact support-foot ownership in source sprites

principle.name: PIN THE TOOL DURING FORCE; BREAK THE JOIN BEFORE RECOVERY
principle.summary: A sustained powered strike can read as a two-stage event: first the tool establishes the line, then the body continues to spend force behind a relatively stable endpoint. Recovery begins by disengaging the tool relation before the torso and root return to neutral.
principle.minimal_maximal_unit: one generic nine-key powered-tool strike showing anticipation, brace, entry, a short pinned-contact phase, explicit disengagement, recoil, and recovery
principle.negative_space: Anticipation reserves a forward corridor. Entry fills it. The contact interval keeps the forward endpoint stable while body spacing compresses behind it. Disengagement restores tool clearance before the body re-expands into recovery.

vocabulary.TWOS: hold one key/drawing for two display frames
vocabulary.FOURS: hold one key/drawing for four display frames
vocabulary.STREET_FIGHTER_CAPCOM: nonuniform inferred gameplay timing with readable anticipation/recovery holds and fast causal transitions

keys.name: READY
keys.motion_arc_root_note: root centered; tool carried close enough to preserve forward negative space

keys.name: ANTICIPATE
keys.motion_arc_root_note: pelvis lowers and shifts back; elbows fold; forward corridor opens before commitment

keys.name: BRACE
keys.motion_arc_root_note: stance widens; shoulders align behind the tool axis; root stays behind the hands

keys.name: ENTRY
keys.motion_arc_root_note: hands and tool accelerate farther than pelvis; silhouette becomes sharply forward-biased

keys.name: ENGAGE
keys.motion_arc_root_note: tool endpoint reaches maximum corridor claim; contact is an inferred demonstration state, not source-observed

keys.name: PRESS
keys.motion_arc_root_note: tool tip remains pinned while pelvis and shoulders compress one cell farther behind it; force spends through body without extending the endpoint

keys.name: DISENGAGE
keys.motion_arc_root_note: tool endpoint retracts off the contact line while torso remains committed; the causal join ends before body recovery

keys.name: RECOIL
keys.motion_arc_root_note: elbows fold and tool shortens further; pelvis begins restack only after clearance is regained

keys.name: RECOVER
keys.motion_arc_root_note: root and shoulders restack after tool clearance; readable ready state and forward negative space are restored

motion_dungeon.interpolation: linear joint geometry only within identical rig topology; ENGAGE, PRESS, and DISENGAGE boundaries snap so contact state is never invented by a transition
